name: Sherwood
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Sherwood, OR 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Sherwood, OR: the Holiday Festival parade and tree lighting, Santa's Christmas Cottage in Old Town and Breakfast with Santa.
lede: Sherwood celebrates Christmas in its nine-block Old Town, where the Robin Hood Festival Association leads a parade to Cannery Square Park for the tree lighting and Santa's Christmas Cottage fills a front porch with elf portals and a Toy Chute.
celebrates: The Sherwood Robin Hood Festival Association hosts the Sherwood Holiday Festival on the first Saturday in December, with a parade from SW 12th Street and Sherwood Boulevard to Cannery Square Park, a tree lighting with school choirs, a Santa tent and free hot dogs, cookies and hot chocolate while supplies last. In Old Town, Santa's Christmas Cottage on SW 1st Street runs a free front porch experience through Christmas Day. Langer's Entertainment Center serves Breakfast with Santa, and the Sherwood Center for the Arts hosts a December series called Winter at the Center.
lastyear: In 2025 the Sherwood Holiday Festival was on Saturday, December 6. The parade started at 4 pm near SW 12th Street and Sherwood Boulevard with the Sherwood High School Marching Band, the Maid Marian Court and Santa, and the tree lighting followed at 5 pm in Cannery Square Park, with the Mixolydians and the Sherwood High School Chorus singing and City Council President Kim Young leading the countdown.
facts: Sherwood began as Smockville. In 1885 J.C. Smock granted the railroad a right of way through his land, and in 1889 he and his wife Mary Ellen Sebastion laid out and named the streets around the tracks. Its community tree lighting was revived in 1984 by the Robin Hood Festival Association, which found that the old holder for a tree in the middle of SW Washington and First Streets was still there.
trains: Sherwood grew up around the railroad after J.C. Smock granted the right of way in 1885, and the town's streets were laid out around the tracks. The Southern Pacific Red Electric later ran passenger service through Sherwood and Newberg. Today the closest TriMet rail is WES Commuter Rail, a weekday line serving Beaverton, Tigard, Tualatin and Wilsonville. In Portland, families can ride the Holiday Express at the Oregon Rail Heritage Center and the Washington Park and Zoo Railway.

traditions: A parade with the high school marching band and the Maid Marian Court ends at Cannery Square Park for the tree lighting.
A free Old Town front porch with a Nice-O-Meter, Elf Portal, Elf Name Generator and Toy Chute.
At the festival, the Junior Maid Marian Court serves as Santa's elves and kids get a free Santa bag while supplies last.
A breakfast buffet with Santa plus laser tag, bowling and the rock wall.
The Sherwood Center for the Arts fills December with holiday shows, crafts and a Christmas sing-along.

kidfact: Sherwood used to be called Smockville, after J.C. Smock, who laid out the town's streets around the railroad tracks in 1889.
faq: When is the Sherwood Holiday Festival in 2026?

The Sherwood Robin Hood Festival Association holds the Holiday Festival on Saturday, December 5, 2026, starting at 4 pm with a parade from SW 12th Street and Sherwood Boulevard to Cannery Square Park, followed by the tree lighting with local school choirs, a visit from Santa and a sing-along with the Maid Marian Court.
Where is Santa's Christmas Cottage in Sherwood?

At the Gardner Team Real Estate office, 16227 SW 1st Street in Old Town. The front porch experience runs from November 23 through December 25, and the organizers describe it as a free community event. The Toy Chute is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 5 pm.
Is there a Breakfast with Santa in Sherwood?

Yes. Langer's Entertainment Center holds Breakfast with Santa on Saturday, December 5, and Sunday, December 6, 2026, from 8 to 11 am. General admission is $25 and includes the buffet, Santa and unlimited attractions until 11 am.
Is there free food at the Sherwood Holiday Festival?

Yes. The Robin Hood Festival Association serves free hot dogs and cookies, with help from the Boy Scouts, plus complimentary hot chocolate and coffee, all while supplies last. Kids who visit the Santa tent also get a free Santa surprise bag donated by local businesses, while supplies last.
Did trains ever run to Sherwood?

Yes. J.C. Smock granted the railroad a right of way through his land in 1885, and the town grew around the tracks. The Southern Pacific Red Electric later carried passengers through Sherwood and Newberg.
